name: acad-geometry-3d
description: AutoCAD 3D solids and surfaces: create primitive solids (box, sphere, cylinder, cone, wedge, torus, pyramid), build solids by extruding or revolving closed planar curves, build planar surfaces (Region) from boundary curves, and query 3D mass properties (volume, surface area via Brep, centroid, principal moments and radii of gyration) plus axis-aligned 3D bounding boxes. All write operations require the AcadMcp .NET plugin loaded inside an open AutoCAD session (NETLOAD or auto-bundle); read-only query tools are flagged ReadOnly = true. Not supported on AutoCAD LT.
intent_examples: cylinder by base radius and height
make a pipe from a profile
sweep a profile along a path

tools_summary.name: draw_box
tools_summary.description: Create a 3D solid box defined by two opposite corner points (axis-aligned in WCS).

tools_summary.name: draw_cone
tools_summary.description: Create a 3D solid cone or frustum (set topRadius>0 for frustum).

tools_summary.name: draw_cylinder
tools_summary.description: Create a 3D solid cylinder by base center, radius, and height (Z+).
intent: cylinder by base radius and height

tools_summary.name: draw_helix
tools_summary.description: Draw a helix - the usual path for a spring, a thread or a spiral stair, and the natural companion to sweep_curve. Give the base centre, a base radius, the height and the number of turns; topRadius makes it taper, and height 0 makes a flat spiral. The result carries expectedLength for a constant-radius helix, worked from the unrolled right triangle - the circumference walked against the height climbed - so the curve can be checked against arithmetic rather than against a second opinion from the same code.

tools_summary.name: draw_planar_surface
tools_summary.description: Create a planar surface entity from one or more closed planar boundary curves (handles).

tools_summary.name: draw_pyramid
tools_summary.description: Create a 3D solid pyramid or frustum with N sides (3..32). Use topRadius>0 for frustum.

tools_summary.name: draw_sphere
tools_summary.description: Create a 3D solid sphere by center point and radius.

tools_summary.name: draw_torus
tools_summary.description: Create a 3D solid torus by center, major (tube path) radius and minor (tube) radius.

tools_summary.name: draw_wedge
tools_summary.description: Create a 3D solid wedge (right-angle prism) defined by two opposite corners.

tools_summary.name: extrude_curve
tools_summary.description: Extrude a closed planar curve (Polyline / Region / Circle) into a 3D solid by given height with optional taper angle in degrees.

tools_summary.name: get_3d_bounding_box
tools_summary.description: Return the axis-aligned 3D bounding box of an entity (min and max points).

tools_summary.name: get_3d_centroid
tools_summary.description: Return the centroid (center of mass) of a 3D solid in WCS coordinates.

tools_summary.name: get_mass_properties
tools_summary.description: Return full mass properties of a 3D solid: volume, surface area, centroid, principal moments and radii of gyration.

tools_summary.name: get_surface_area
tools_summary.description: Return total surface area of a 3D solid or surface.

tools_summary.name: get_volume
tools_summary.description: Return the volume of a 3D solid (single value, current units).

tools_summary.name: loft_curves
tools_summary.description: Run a solid skin between two or more cross sections - AutoCAD's LOFT. Optionally follow guide curves OR a path, which are alternatives and cannot both be given. ruled=true joins the sections with straight sides instead of a smooth skin; closed=true runs the skin back from the last section to the first. The result lists each section's area, so the volume can be checked against them: two equal sections a distance apart make a prism of area times distance, and a taper makes less.

tools_summary.name: revolve_curve
tools_summary.description: Revolve a closed planar curve around an arbitrary axis (axisStart, axisEnd) by angle in degrees (default 360).

tools_summary.name: sweep_curve
tools_summary.description: Sweep a closed profile along a path curve to make a 3D solid - AutoCAD's SWEEP. extrude_curve pushes a profile in a straight line; this carries it along a line, arc, polyline, spline or helix, which is how a pipe, a handrail or a moulding is modelled. align='path' keeps the profile square to the path as it turns, which is almost always what you want. The result reports the profile area, the path length and their product, so the volume can be checked against arithmetic: a profile carried square along a STRAIGHT path encloses exactly area times length, and the two diverge as the path bends.
intent: sweep a profile along a path
make a pipe from a profile
